channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Farmers Seek Sunflower Import Ban Amid Record Harvest Expectations
item.description: Kazakh farmers are anticipating a record sunflower harvest and are proposing a ban on imports from Russia. They are concerned that cheap Russian sunflower oil could depress domestic prices, which are already showing signs of pressure. Experts suggest government intervention to prevent market disruption.

item.title: French Experts Assess Kazakhstan's Role in Central Asian Modernization
item.description: French experts have positively evaluated Kazakhstan's ongoing political and legal reforms. Journalist Radouane Kuraq highlighted Kazakhstan as a model for strengthening the rule of law in Central Asia, citing reforms in parliamentary structure, judiciary, and human rights protection. Geopolitical advisor Sebastien Boussois noted Kazakhstan's significant regional position.

item.title: Astana Declaration on Digital Labor Signed at International Forum
item.description: An international forum in Astana concluded with the signing of the Astana Tripartite Declaration on Digital Labor and Artificial Intelligence. The forum, held in honor of World Day for Decent Work and Trade Union Day, also adopted a Digital Charter for Trade Unions. Discussions focused on developing digital labor market infrastructure and integrating modern technologies.

item.title: Two Workers Die During Water Pipe Replacement in Shymkent
item.description: Two workers have died while replacing water pipes in Shymkent. The incident occurred in a deep well where three employees of a private company were working. Preliminary reports suggest the young men, aged 20-22, may have died from gas poisoning. A criminal investigation has been launched.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Withhold Details of Military Accident Aid to Families
item.description: Kazakhstan will not disclose the amount of aid or personal data of military personnel killed or injured during exercises in the Caspian Sea. This decision was made at the request of relatives to protect privacy, according to Bekmurat Zhusupov, chairman of the Mangystau Public Council. All funds have been distributed according to established procedures.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ranks 34th in World Population Review's Most Powerful Countries Index
item.description: Kazakhstan has been ranked 34th in the World Population Review's 'Most Powerful Countries 2026' index, placing it between Hungary and Egypt. The ranking considers factors like leadership, economic and political influence, international alliances, and military power. Among post-Soviet states, only Russia ranked higher.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Constitutional Reform Strengthens Protection of Citizens' Rights
item.description: Kazakhstan's new Constitution, effective July 1, strengthens the protection of human rights and freedoms. Key changes include enshrining the 'Miranda rule' at the constitutional level and establishing the independent constitutional status of the bar. The reform aims to ensure judicial fairness and enhance legal oversight of state bodies.

item.title: Kazakhstan and South Korea Launch Smart Telemedicine Project
item.description: A telemedicine center utilizing artificial intelligence has been launched at the Mangystau Regional Multidisciplinary Hospital in Kazakhstan. The center will enable early diagnosis, identification of complex diseases, and remote consultations with foreign specialists. The initiative was announced at an international symposium in Aktau.

item.title: Doctor Arrested in Bukhara for Taking $500 for Medical Certificate
item.description: A doctor from a family polyclinic in Bukhara, Uzbekistan, has been arrested for allegedly accepting $500. The doctor reportedly promised to prepare a medical certificate for a citizen to obtain an academic leave from their educational institution. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Competition Committee investigates justification for mobile operator tariff increases
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has launched an investigation into the justification for upcoming mobile operator tariff hikes. Consumers have complained about rising prices without guaranteed service quality, limited data usage, and non-transferable unused internet. The committee will take action if anti-competitive practices or consumer rights violations are found.

item.title: Pakistan's Shifting Support for Afghan Groups Analyzed
item.description: Pakistan's support for Afghan groups has historically been interest-driven, shifting based on their effectiveness in achieving strategic objectives. This pattern, evident since the 1990s and during the Cold War, saw Pakistan back Mujahideen, then the Taliban, and later ally with the US against the Taliban. The text suggests a historical tendency to withdraw support when backed groups lose effectiveness.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Cooperation with Green Climate Fund
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing its collaboration with the Green Climate Fund. A regional dialogue in Tbilisi focused on climate finance, investment project preparation, and strengthening regional cooperation. Uzbekistan emphasized moving from strategic dialogue to concrete investment initiatives, proposing enhanced regional cooperation in areas like early warning systems, data exchange, water management, and decarbonization.

item.title: Astana Increases Bus Numbers on 16 City Routes
item.description: Astana is increasing the number of buses on 16 city routes to improve transport services. An additional 22 buses will be added to 11 routes and 10 buses to 5 express routes. These changes, implemented from October 10 and 12, aim to reduce waiting times and enhance passenger convenience.

item.title: Taliban Ministry Claims Seizure of 50 Hectares of Land in Balkh Province
item.description: Afghanistan's Taliban Ministry of Justice announced the seizure of approximately 50 hectares of land in Balkh Province, including farms in Mazar-e-Sharif. The ministry stated that a special court reviewed documents related to the land. The Taliban have claimed numerous properties since regaining control.

item.title: UN Expresses Concern Over Arrests of Women and Girls in Afghanistan by De Facto Authorities
item.description: The UN Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) is deeply concerned about the arrest and detention of women and girls by the country's de facto authorities. Between July and September 2026, at least 52 women and one girl were arrested in Herat and Kabul, often for dress code violations or appearing in public without a male guardian. UNAMA stated these actions violate women's rights and called for an end to discriminatory practices.

item.title: Taliban Report 678 Migrants Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 678 migrants, comprising 163 families, were forcibly returned to Afghanistan. Spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that arrivals occurred through Torkham, Silk Bridge, Spin Boldak, and Islam Qala border crossings across Nangarhar, Nimroz, Kandahar, and Herat provinces respectively.

item.title: Kazakhstan Commission Reports Fair Distribution of Financial Aid to Families of Deceased Servicemen
item.description: A commission in Kazakhstan's Mangystau region has stated that financial aid to families of deceased and injured servicemen has been distributed fairly and evenly. The head of the commission, Bekmurat Zhusupov, declined to disclose specific payment amounts, citing the wishes of the recipients. The aid was initiated following a presidential directive and funded by contributions from businesses and philanthropists.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Host Belgian King Philippe and Queen Mathilde on State Visit
item.description: Kazakhstan will host King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium for a state visit from October 11 to 14. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation, with discussions planned between the leaders and the signing of international documents. The royal couple's agenda includes participation in a business council meeting and a forum for university rectors.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports Nearly $1 Billion in Financial Losses from Cybercrimes in First Nine Months of 2024
item.description: In the first nine months of 2024, Uzbekistan experienced nearly 1 trillion Uzbek soums (approximately $98 million) in financial losses due to cybercrimes. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the majority of the 69,962 cybercrimes involved electronic payment systems. Efforts are underway to recover funds, with over 210 billion soums returned to victims.

item.title: US Treasury Issues General License for Operations Involving Russian Diesel Fuel
item.description: The U.S. Treasury Department has issued a general license permitting transactions involving Russian diesel fuel, previously restricted by sanctions. The license, valid until April 7, 2027, allows for the sale, transport, and import of Russian diesel. However, it prohibits transferring funds to Russian state-controlled financial institutions.

item.title: King and Queen of Belgium to Visit Kazakhstan for State Visit
item.description: King Philippe and Queen Mathilde of Belgium will visit Kazakhstan from October 11-14 at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Discussions will focus on strengthening multifaceted cooperation. They will attend a business council meeting and a forum for university rectors.

item.title: King of Belgium to Visit Kazakhstan for State Visit, Talks and Agreements Planned
item.description: King Philippe of Belgium and Queen Mathilde will visit Kazakhstan from October 11-14 at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. High-level talks will focus on developing cooperation. They will attend a business council meeting and a forum for university rectors, with agreements expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ranks Second in Health System Satisfaction in STADA Study
item.description: A STADA Health Report 2026 study revealed that 82% of respondents in Uzbekistan are satisfied with the state healthcare system, significantly above the average of 56%. Uzbekistan ranked second among 20 participating countries, with only Belgium showing higher satisfaction. The study, conducted in February-March, surveyed 19,514 individuals aged 18-99, including over 1,000 from Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. This marks Uzbekistan's fourth participation in the research.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces 14-Day Cooling-Off Period for Unsecured Loans
item.description: Starting October 12, 2026, Kazakhstan will implement a new regulation allowing borrowers to cancel unsecured loans within 14 days of signing the contract. Banks cannot charge penalties for this cancellation, but borrowers must pay for the days they used the funds. A similar right applies to associated voluntary insurance, with a refund of the unused premium. Lenders must inform clients about this right beforehand.

item.title: Turkmenistan Inaugurates New Oncology, Dentistry, and Pediatric Centers
item.description: Turkmenistan has opened new International Oncology, Dentistry, and Pediatric centers, coinciding with the Day of Health and Medical Industry Workers. These facilities are part of a broader national effort to modernize the healthcare system and align medical services with global standards, as outlined in the 'Saglyk' state program. This expansion aims to improve citizen well-being and access to advanced medical care.

item.title: US Temporarily Eases Sanctions on Russian Diesel Amid Supply Deal
item.description: The United States has temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel following an agreement to supply 300,000 tons to the global market. US President Donald Trump stated that Russia plans further deliveries, with potential for an additional 3 million tons depending on refinery conditions. Trump believes increased diesel supply could lower global fuel prices, benefiting consumers and industries. He previously discussed energy supplies with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Special Operations Forces Commander Amidst Military Shake-up
item.description: Kazakhstan has appointed Sayat Isanov as the new commander of the Special Operations Forces of the Armed Forces. This follows a significant reshuffling of leadership within the Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces after a naval exercise tragedy resulted in 14 deaths. The former commander, Aidoss Myrzakhmetov, is now the Minister of Defense. Several officials face charges related to negligence and navigation violations.

item.title: Tajikistan secures first place at XX CIS Youth Delphic Games in Dushanbe
item.description: Tajikistan topped the XX Delphic Games for CIS Youth, held in Dushanbe, winning 16 medals including six gold. Kazakhstan placed second with 11 medals. The event featured participants aged 10-25 from nine countries competing in ten artistic disciplines over five days.

item.title: Water Ministry Comments on Reports of Amu Darya Drying Up
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Water Management has responded to reports claiming the Amu Darya river is drying up. The ministry stated that water flow in the Amu Darya is being maintained. They explained that reduced water levels in rivers during September-October are a seasonal hydrological phenomenon.

item.title: UN Women Executive Director Highlights Over 12 Million Girls Married Annually Before 18
item.description: UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous stated that over 12 million girls worldwide marry before age 18 each year, jeopardizing their rights to education, health, and security. While progress has been made, ending child marriage requires political will, investment, and enforcement of protective laws.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Maximum Interest Rates for Leasing Agreements
item.description: Kazakhstan has set maximum annual effective interest rates for financial leasing agreements, ranging from 35% to 46% depending on property value and lessor type. The order, signed by the Minister of Industry and Construction, specifies rates based on asset value and whether a bank is the lessor.

item.title: 3 MW Solar Power Plant Commissioned in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region
item.description: A 3 MW solar power plant has been officially commissioned in the village of Roj, Shugnan district, Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO), Tajikistan. The facility, built by OJSC "Tajikgidroelektromontazh" in cooperation with South Korea, is located at an altitude of 2,600 meters and covers four hectares. It aims to enhance regional power supply reliability and promote clean energy.

item.title: FlyDubai Co-pilot Planned Terror Attack on Tel Aviv Airport, UAE Prosecutor Claims
item.description: The co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight confessed to planning a terror attack targeting Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv, according to UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al-Shamsi. The Omani national allegedly studied the route and airport during previous flights and attempted to seize control of the aircraft on a third trip, intending to crash it.

item.title: Putin's Plane from Turkmenistan Lands in St. Petersburg Instead of Moscow Amid Drone Alerts
item.description: President Putin's aircraft, an Ilyushin Il-96 that flew to Turkmenistan, landed in St. Petersburg instead of Moscow on October 9. The plane later departed for the capital. The diversion may have been due to drone alerts, as Moscow airports briefly restricted flights.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Withhold Details on Payments to Families of Soldiers Lost at Sea
item.description: Kazakhstan will not disclose the amounts paid to families of military personnel who died or were injured during exercises in the Caspian Sea. This decision was made at the request of the families to ensure confidentiality. The commission has completed its work, and all funds have been distributed. Seventeen servicemen were lost at sea during exercises in September, with 14 fatalities.

item.title: Greek Company Plans to Process Metallurgical Waste in Kazakhstan
item.description: A Greek industrial group, Metlen Energy & Metals, plans to establish metallurgical waste processing in Kazakhstan to extract valuable metals like copper, zinc, and nickel. The project aligns with government priorities on waste recycling and value-added production. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed readiness to facilitate the project's development and cooperation with relevant ministries and companies.

item.title: US and Russia Agree on Diesel Exports to Stabilize Global Prices
item.description: The United States and Russia have reached an agreement for Russia to supply over 300,000 tonnes of diesel to global markets, including the US. President Trump announced the deal, aimed at reducing fuel prices. The US has also temporarily suspended restrictions on Russian fuel imports. Further supplies are planned for November and December.

item.title: US Temporarily Eases Sanctions on Russian Fuel to Lower Global Prices
item.description: The United States has temporarily eased sanctions on Russian fuel following an agreement for Russia to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the global market. President Trump stated this decision aims to reduce rising diesel prices, which impact agriculture, heating, and transportation. The move comes ahead of midterm elections.

item.title: Iran Proposes New 'CIS+1' Format for Deeper Cooperation with Commonwealth States
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian proposed establishing a 'CIS+1' format to deepen Tehran's engagement with Commonwealth of Independent States members. Speaking at the CIS summit, he emphasized regional diplomacy's role in crisis resolution and conflict prevention. Iran sees itself as a bridge between Central Asia and open seas.

item.title: Gold Bars Worth $40 Million Confiscated at China Border, Smuggled by Kyrgyz Citizen
item.description: Kazakhstan's court confiscated six gold bars valued at 182.3 million tenge (approximately $40 million) that a citizen of Kyrgyzstan attempted to smuggle into China. The woman hid the bars, weighing 2.8 kilograms, under her shoe insoles. The gold, exceeding 99% purity, was seized at the Khorgos border crossing.
